gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two BLUETTI SP200L panels in BLUETTI's own Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W kit have to be wired in series. In series they make 49.2 V open-circuit, inside the station's 12–60 V window. In parallel they make 21.6 A short-circuit, over its 20 A maximum. A third panel fits neither way (73.8 V in series, 32.4 A in parallel), so the store's 3-panel option is too much for this station.
standout_why: Eco Solar Kits (cited) gives no panel Voc, no input voltage window and no series/parallel advice. It only says same-brand folding panels 'plug straight in, with no adapters'. On this kit that is incomplete: the station's box lists only an AC cable, and the panels connect by MC4. Wattfolk (cited) says to 'wire in series for 24V or in parallel for 12V' for an ECO-WORTHY kit and tells readers to check the station's input limits, but gives no numbers. Its 12 V-kit habit of parallel wiring is the wrong choice here. AgriPure (cited) could not be read: WebFetch failed with an SSL certificate error and the curl fallback was not approved. Its coverage of this is unchecked. None of the pages I read does Voc/Isc arithmetic against a named station's input window.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W AC). Its solar input is 12–60 V and 20 A max, up to 1,000 W. That takes two SP200L panels in series (49.2 V, 10.8 A).
Solar panels: 2× BLUETTI SP200L 200 W (MC4, Voc 24.6 V, Isc 10.8 A). Two in series sit inside the station's window. Two in parallel go over the 20 A cap. Do not add a third panel.

Cable: BLUETTI Solar Charging Cable (20A MC4 to XT60). The Elite 200 V2 box lists only the unit, an AC charging cable, a grounding screw and documentation. I did not open a page confirming the station's solar port is XT60, so check this before relying on it.

findings.note: Arithmetic: 2 × 24.6 V = 49.2 V, which is under the 60 V maximum. Current stays at 10.8 A, which is under 20 A.

findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Portable Power Station (US store), FAQ Q1
findings.note: Arithmetic: 2 × 10.8 A = 21.6 A, which is more than the station's 20 A max.

findings.label: Third panel fits neither way
findings.value: 73.8 V in series (over 60 V); 32.4 A in parallel (over 20 A)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI 200W Portable Solar Panel (US store), sold in 1-, 2- and 3-panel versions
findings.note: Arithmetic: 3 × 24.6 V = 73.8 V; 3 × 10.8 A = 32.4 A. The store sells a 3×200 W version for $1,197, but on one Elite 200 V2 input the most these panels can supply is 2 in series, 400 W.
